commits.pr_title: [ROCm][RDNA3] Fix W4A16 split-K accuracy and determinism
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

The RDNA3 (gfx11) W4A16 GPTQ kernels accumulate split-K partials in
bf16/fp16 via CAS atomics. The narrowing happens **before** accumulation,
and low-precision addition is not associative — so whichever split block
wins the CAS first changes the result. That numerical error is present on
**every affected forward pass**, in every decoding configuration.

Greedy decoding is merely where it becomes visible: at temperature 0 the
rounded logit wobble can flip `argmax` between repeated identical
generations (the trail in #50603). Under sampling (e.g. T=0.6) the same
error hides under the sampler's own noise while still sitting under every
reported metric.

## Root cause

```
FP32 per-block partial
  -> bf16/fp16 narrowing (8 / 11 mantissa bits)
  -> CAS-atomic accumulation in execution-dependent order
```

gfx11 has no packed bf16/fp16 atomic, so the epilogue emulated one with a
CAS retry loop — which also made the accumulation order scheduler- and
contention-dependent.

## Fix

Keep the compute kernels and dispatch unchanged; replace only the epilogue
on both paths:

```
FP32 per-split partials
  -> fixed ascending-z FP32 reduction
  -> one final bf16/fp16 cast
```

* Every path writes each output element exactly once; `k_split == 1`
  (WMMA) and `z_count == 1` (scalar) keep/store directly — no scratch, no
  reduce, no atomics.
* The FP32 partials scratch is `at::empty`: coverage is total by
  construction (every reducer-visible `(z, m, n)` slot has exactly one
  writer in all seven WMMA variants and the scalar kernel; the invariant
  is documented at `alloc_wmma_partials`), so there is no zero-fill pass.
* Scratch is per-call via the caching allocator, row-tiled so the bound is
  independent of the caller's M.

## Accuracy (W7900/gfx1100, FP32 dequantized reference)

Max abs error, synthetic uint4b8/group-128 weights, K=4096:

| path | dtype | legacy CAS | this PR | factor |
|------|-------|-----------:|--------:|-------:|
| scalar | bf16 | 0.24–0.37 | 0.0625 | 4–6x |
| WMMA | bf16 | 0.15–0.23 | 0.09–0.11 | ~2x |
| WMMA | fp16 | 0.024–0.038 | 0.011–0.018 | ~2x |
| scalar | fp16 | ~0.95 | 0.002-0.015 | **94-201x** (see 2026-10-01 update: exact factored dequant) |

bf16 is the headline; fp16 carried 11 mantissa bits so the removed CAS
rounding cost it ~8x less (as expected). The scalar-fp16 row was the
classic exllama bit-trick rounding the per-group offset constant to fp16
— fixed by the exact factored dequant in the 2026-10-01 update below
(now 0.002-0.015 on the same shapes).

The earlier "0.028 → 0.0061" measurement is the same bf16 improvement
factor on real Muse weights. bf16 residual error now sits at the final
output cast (1 ulp); WMMA at the B-tile narrowing.

## Determinism

Fixed inputs now produce bit-identical outputs on every call: 20/20
benchmark shapes repeatable; real Muse q_proj at M=1 gives 1 distinct
result / 100 calls (previously up to 200/200 distinct). Repeatability
alone is not correctness, so the tests also check values against the FP32
reference — a stale `at::empty` scratch slot would be bitwise-repeatable
and wrong, and is caught by the tolerance analysis in the test module.

## Performance (W7900/gfx1100, median of 100 CUDA-event timings)

Rows are **bf16**; fp16 differs in dispatch (bf16 reaches WMMA at
M ≥ 16, fp16 not until M ≥ 64 — at M=16 fp16 is still on the scalar path):

| M | N | K | path | k_split | scratch MB | before µs | after µs | Δ |
|--:|---:|---:|------|--------:|-----------:|----------:|---------:|---:|
| 1 | 4096 | 4096 | scalar | 16 | 0.25 | 44.5 | 39.7 | -10.8% |
| 8 | 4096 | 4096 | scalar | 16 | 2.0 | 61.8 | 57.2 | -7.5% |
| 16 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 16x16_1w | 4 | 1.0 | 58.8 | 53.7 | **-8.7%** |
| 64 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 64x64_4w | 4 | 4.0 | 120.5 | 112.0 | **-7.0%** |
| 128 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 8.0 | 123.5 | 114.7 | **-7.2%** |
| 512 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 32.0 | 378.4 | 350.8 | **-7.3%** |
| 512 | 4096 | 6656 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 32.0 | 554.7 | 527.4 | -4.9% |
| 512 | 25600 | 6656 | wmma 128x64_k32 | **1** | **0** | 3070.7 | 2894.2 | -5.8% |

(Historical W7900 campaign numbers; superseded WMMA-dispatch note: fp16
now reaches WMMA from M>=12, see the 2026-10-01 update.)
Full tables for both dtypes incl. N/K/k_split/scratch
per row: `05-benchmark.md` in the evidence package:
https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/evidence/pr-54706-jartx-w7900/validation-54706-jartx-w7900
(immutable: same tree at commit
https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/9bc79045c157dd12a2728cad4e52fd9b21b0ccc3/validation-54706-jartx-w7900)

Notes:
- "before" = this branch's original HEAD (zero-filled WMMA scratch);
  "after" = with the dead zero-fill removed (`at::zeros` → `at::empty`
  once total coverage was proven). Same-M/different-N matters: at M=512,
  N=4096 → k_split=4 (32 MB scratch) while N=25600 → k_split=1 (none).
- Versus a locally restored legacy-CAS control build, the deterministic
  epilogue is now at parity or **faster** for prefill shapes (bf16 M=16:
  53.7 vs 55.3 µs); only M=1 decode pays a residual ~4–10% (scratch
  round-trip at tiny output) — the price of bit-reproducibility.
- Numerics are bit-identical before/after the memset removal on all 20
  shapes (zero-init was dead traffic).
- A follow-up fix (CodeRabbit finding) gave the V7/V8 k_split==1 path
  the same direct-store branch the 64x64 path had: no scratch, no
  reduce, partials == nullptr. N=25600 row: bf16 3020.1 -> 2894.2 µs
  (-4.2%), fp16 2858.3 -> 2668.6 µs (-6.6%); split-K shapes unchanged
  within noise; numerics bit-identical.

## Why not FP32 atomics?

gfx11 does have `global_atomic_add_f32`; an FP32 scratch accumulated with
native atomics plus one cast pass would remove nearly all the rounding
error with no reduce kernel. We still chose the fixed-order reduce:
FP32 addition is also non-associative, so atomic accumulation remains
order-dependent — vastly better numerically, but not bit-reproducible.
Since bit-exact reproducibility is an explicit goal of this PR, the
fixed ascending-z reduction is the design that guarantees it.

## Tests

`tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_w4a16_determinism.py` — 24 tests:

* bit-repeatability through the public op (scalar/WMMA × bf16/fp16),
  with the scalar regression at K=4096 (16 concurrent writers — well
  inside the old failure regime, whose onset was 2–4 writers);
* FP32-reference correctness for scalar and WMMA, split-K and
  direct-store (k_split == 1 / z_count == 1) paths, both dtypes, with
  tolerances derived from each path's rounding structure;
* explicit V7/V8 (128x64) no-split coverage at M=512, N=25600, K=6656
  (repeatability + FP32 reference, both dtypes; routing asserted via a
  replica of the k_split heuristic);
* test hygiene: repo-standard `dist_init` fixture (no `__enter__` leak,
  no hardcoded MASTER_PORT).

On a locally restored legacy-CAS build, 8 tests fail (7 repeatability +
the scalar-bf16 reference check at max_abs 0.30 vs 0.10 tolerance,
measured on the then-20-test suite); on this PR, 24/24 pass.

## Validation

- W7900D / gfx1100, ROCm 7.14 runtime, torch 2.14; upstream base
  `40b2f62061575905aaac8bc360eaea62a4baeb67`
- targeted tests 24/24 PASS (bf16 + fp16, scalar + WMMA, incl. V7/V8
  no-split)
- FP32-reference correctness + A/B legacy control: see above
- benchmark matrix: dtype × M{1,8,16,64,128,512} × N{4096,25600} ×
  K{4096,6656} with path/k_split/scratch per row (full evidence package
  below)
- independent RX 7900 XT evidence from @cadamcat (A/B table in #50603)
- full W7900/gfx1100 reproducibility package (environment, correctness
  and A/B-control evidence, complete benchmark tables):
  https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/evidence/pr-54706-jartx-w7900/validation-54706-jartx-w7900
- Muse eager ctx512: 1 unique / 8 greedy generations; 0
  same-input/different-output events across 16,640 intercepted W4A16
  GEMM calls

## Scope

gfx11 / RDNA3 W4A16 only; no attention-routing changes. The residual
Muse eager/8192 divergence after this fix was traced to ROCm paged
attention V-cache tail consumption and is fixed by #53856. Investigation
trail: #50603; full earlier evidence in the
`validation-50603/rdna3-w4a16-upstream-cleanup` tree linked there.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used for code iteration, validation orchestration, and
drafting. I reviewed the final diff, kernel behavior, test results,
performance data, and evidence and can explain the change end to end.




---

## Rebase validation (2026-09-09, post-#54809)

Rebased onto upstream/main `385dce36` after #54809 (GPTQ act-order/g_idx
removal) and revalidated on gfx1100 (W7900D, torch 2.14.0+rocm7.14,
ROCm 7.2.1 toolchain — same environment as the original campaign):

- conflicts resolved semantically; the post-#54809 no-g_idx op contract
  (`gptq_gemm_rdna3(a, b_q_weight, b_qzeros, b_scales, use_v2_format)`)
  kept native — no `b_g_idx`/`b_q_perm`/`has_g_idx`/`w_gidx_param_name`
  anywhere in the PR
- gfx1100 build PASS; gfx942 (non-RDNA3 stub pass) compile guard PASS
- targeted determinism/FP32-reference suite: **24/24 PASS**
- upstream RDNA3 tests (`test_rdna3_w4a16`, `test_rdna3_compile_guards`,
  `test_rdna3_w4a16_selection`, `test_rdna3_moe_w4a16`): 148 passed,
  5 skipped (non-gfx1100 guards), 0 failed
- V7/V8 `k_split == 1` direct-store confirmed (no scratch, no reducer,
  profiler-verified); split-K control: deterministic FP32 reducer active,
  scratch 33.6 MB as designed; scalar z_count=1/z_count=16 paths verified
- performance within noise of the pre-rebase reference:
  no-split M=512 N=25600 K=6656 — bf16 2877 µs / fp16 2633 µs (was
  2894 / 2669); split-K M=512 N=4096 K=6656 — bf16 545 µs / fp16 507 µs
  (was ~528 / ~501); scratch 0 / 33.6 MB unchanged
- DCO green on all replayed commits; historical W7900 measurements above
  remain the pre-rebase evidence package (unchanged)

Note: the two commits added on top of the original six adapt the tests to
the post-#54809 API and apply the repo's current formatter pins
(ruff 0.14.0 / clang-format 21.1.2); no semantic changes.


## Update (2026-10-01): exact fp16 dequant, M>=12 WMMA dispatch, fused fp16 split-K reduce

Addressed @JartX's two review items (semantically ported from
dafcde3f8bb9 and 5e8db861e02 — neither cherry-picks cleanly) and rebased
onto current upstream/main `ccda9098`.

### 1. fp16 dequant is now exact (the "~0.95" row is gone)

The old bit-trick bakes `z = scale * (-1024 - zero)` into an **fp16**
constant; that representation rounding (~0.008 abs at scale≈0.02, repeated
for every weight of a group×column) was the error — not the epilogue. The
dequant now uses the exact factored form

```
sum_k a_k * w_k  =  y * sum_k a_k * (1024 + q_k)  +  z * sum_k a_k
```

with **fp32** (y, z) pairs per nibble slot and the z·sum_a correction
applied once per 32-K round (same structure the bf16 path already had).
Ported to the dense scalar kernel **and** the MoE kernel (its baked error
was previously masked by the dense reference being equally biased).

Accuracy vs the FP32 dequantized reference on gfx1100 (public op path,
100-repeat calls, K=4096–6656, M=1/4/8):

| path | dtype | before | after | factor |
|------|-------|-------:|------:|-------:|
| scalar | fp16 | 1.03–1.37 | 0.002–0.015 | **94–201x** |
| scalar | bf16 | 0.06–0.12 | 0.06–0.12 | bit-identical (unchanged) |

### 2. WMMA dispatch: both dtypes from M ≥ 12

Measured scalar/WMMA crossover on this gfx1100 (both ops timed directly,
identical inputs, median of 300; full table in the dispatch comment): at
M ≥ 12 WMMA wins or ties on every measured shape for both dtypes
(1.00–1.69x); below that scalar wins and is the more accurate path. fp16
previously stayed scalar until M=64 — that speed came with ~100x more
dequant error; with the exact dequant the crossover moved to 12, same as
bf16. An M=11 (scalar) / M=12 (WMMA) boundary test pins it via profiler
kernel names.

### 3. Split-K reduction fused into the fp16 kernel — with per-call state

The fp16 scalar path now reduces in the GEMM kernel: each block publishes
arrival on its tile's ticket; the last z block sums the z-slices in fixed
ascending order (batched loads) and rounds once — still bit-reproducible,
one launch fewer, partials read while L2-hot.

**The ticket array is per-call** (`at::zeros`, one int per tile,
re-armed in-kernel), **not** the device-global `g_w4_tickets` of the
reference: nothing in vLLM serializes quantized W4A16 GEMMs on one device
(DeepSeek V4/V4.1 aux-stream forks, LoRA dual-stream, and the
SharedExperts side stream all overlap quantized linears today), so
cross-launch global state would be a correctness hazard. Per-call tickets
from the stream-aware caching allocator keep concurrent invocations
independent by construction; verified by a two-stream concurrent-vs-serial
(bit-exact) test and CUDA-graph capture/replay tests.

The **bf16** path keeps the separate reducer: measured on gfx1100, fusing
it was neutral at M=1 and up to ~10% slower at M=4–8 (the fused reduce
serializes a multi-row tile's reduction into one block per tile), so bf16
behavior is unchanged.

Performance, interleaved A/B/C in one session (original baked / exact +
separate reduce / final; min of 4-rep medians × 3 rounds; public op):

| dtype | M | vs original | vs separate-reduce |
|-------|--:|------------:|-------------------:|
| fp16 | 1 | **−6.3 … −11.3%** | −8.1 … −8.8% |
| fp16 | 4 | −6.7 … −8.2% | −11 … −12% |
| fp16 | 8 | −2.2 … −7.6% | −6 … −16% |
| bf16 | 1–8 | −1.4 … +0.1% (noise) | — (unchanged path) |

i.e. the final fp16 kernel is both ~100–200x more accurate **and**
6–11% faster at decode than the pre-review state.

### Validation (gfx1100 / ROCm 7.2.1 toolchain, torch 2.13.0+rocm7.14, base `ccda9098`)

- targeted determinism/reference suite: **54/54 PASS** (fp16+bf16, scalar+
  WMMA, split-K z∈{2,16,17,26} incl. K%256≠0 clipped tails, no-split,
  G∈{32,64,128}, M_COUNT∈{1,2,4,8}, M=100 multi-row-tile, dispatch
  boundary, 100x repeats, two-stream, graph capture/replay)
- upstream RDNA3 suites (`test_rdna3_w4a16`, `_compile_guards`,
  `_selection`, `_moe_w4a16`): **151 passed, 5 skipped** (non-gfx1100
  guards), 0 failed
- gfx942 full build PASS; RDNA3 ops confirmed absent from the gfx942
  binary (compile guard)
- non-RDNA3 stub updated for the new kernel parameter

### Scope notes

- The MoE kernel gets the **exact dequant** (its tests compare against the
  dense op, which is now exact) but keeps its existing epilogue; making
  the MoE split-K deterministic is follow-up work.
- `groupsize % 32 == 0` is now stated where assumed and host-enforced
  (dense + MoE) — such configs were silently wrong before (the kernel
  checks group transitions at 32-K granularity); K % 32 ≠ 0 remains a
  pre-existing upstream limitation, unchanged here.
- The legacy CAS epilogues stay for A/B comparison, clearly marked; the
  shipped dispatch never selects them.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Keep discovery heartbeats running while workers hold the GIL
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Keep MoRIIO discovery registration alive during worker GIL holds and temporary
router outages. Report unexpected heartbeat subprocess exit through worker
completion polling. This independent fix was extracted from #58968, which no
longer contains the implementation; it has no dependency on the K3 data path.

## Claims

```text
rank-0 worker -> heartbeat subprocess -> unchanged MessagePack registration
  temporary send timeout -> retry until the worker exits
  unexpected child exit -> worker get_finished() raises with its exit code
  worker shutdown / parent pipe EOF -> stop and reap the child
```

## Validation

- **Before:** main's actual threaded sender fails the 300 ms GIL-hold test.
  At pre-review HEAD `512a877511`, the new router-outage test fails to resume
  registration; killing the child or ending its input pipe leaves worker
  completion polling silent (**3 failed**).
- **After:** **46 passed, 0 skipped** across the existing proxy-routing and
  MoRIIO TP-ACK suites. Tests use real subprocesses and loopback ZeroMQ for
  GIL independence, initial registration, router disappearance until the send
  queue times out, registration after the router returns, parent death,
  repeated shutdown, and propagation of both signal and zero-code child exits.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy 3.10, and manual mypy 3.12 passed.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_heartbeat.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_heartbeat.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py
```

Validation covers process and worker lifecycle on CPU. No model-output,
accuracy, throughput, or end-to-end model-serving result is claimed for this
isolated control-plane change.

## Details

The finite retry limit previously treated ZeroMQ send timeouts during temporary
disconnection as terminal. Those timeouts now retry for the worker lifetime;
other repeated ZMQ errors still terminate the child. The parent previously
never inspected child status. It now checks on each worker completion poll,
including unexpected exit code zero. An idle worker observes a fatal child
exit when it next polls; this does not introduce a background restart manager.

**Door:** Two-way. Reverting restores the threaded sender without changing the
discovery wire format. **Blast radius:** MoRIIO workers with a discovery proxy.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, extraction and PR preparation.

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Per-row candidate IDs for prefill token scoring (M2 of #56860)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

M2 of #56860, following #54335. `SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids` becomes per row: one candidate list per scored causal prompt row, so an on-policy distillation teacher scores each response position against the student's own top-K.

- **Input**: an integer array `[num_rows, num_ids]` (or nested lists), `-1` padding shorter rows. Row `j` scores prompt token `prompt_logprob_start + j + 1`; the row count must equal `prompt_len - 1 - prompt_logprob_start`.
- **Output**: unchanged shape, `[num_rows, num_ids]` float32; padded entries are `-inf`, as decode-side `logprob_token_ids` pads.

This replaces the request-wise form; the same IDs at every row is a tiled array.

## Design

- **Array, not nested lists.** The table is normalized once in `verify()` (before the processor's deepcopy) to C-contiguous `int32`, like the runner's other token ID buffers, and travels on the existing zero-copy ndarray path. Measured against an all-`list[list[int]]` prototype: 4000 × 64 costs +5 ms vs +105 ms, 4000 × 1024 +9 ms vs +1.6 s.
- **JSON.** The field is `Annotated[np.ndarray, GetPydanticSchema(... list[list[StrictInt]])]`; `PydanticMsgspecMixin` now keeps `Annotated` metadata (`include_extras=True`). `SamplingParams` is the mixin's only user and no other field's schema changes.
- **Validation.** `verify()` checks shape, width (`--max-logprobs`) and a `max_model_len` row bound before padding, then vocabulary; admission checks the exact row count against the prompt.
- **Worker.** The table is sliced per prefill chunk by absolute prompt row; `-1` is clamped for the gather and masked to `-inf` at emit; state is freed once scores are emitted.
- **Rust frontend** (`/inference/v1/generate`): parses `Vec<Vec<i32>>`, applies the same checks in the same order, and sends an `int32` ndarray (aux frame when large). The checks are required there: engine-core does not re-validate.

## Test Plan

GB200, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` with this branch overlaid, `vllm-rs` built from this branch.

- `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k prompt_logprob_token_ids`, `test_logprobs_processor.py`, `test_trace_replay_params.py`: 6 passed. The chunked-prefill + preemption test uses distinct candidates per row and checks them against an unchunked run and same-run `prompt_logprobs`.
- `test_serving_tokens.py::test_generate_prompt_token_id_logprobs`, Python and Rust frontends: passed.
- `vllm serve` (Qwen3-0.6B, chunked prefill at 64 tokens), 36 cases per frontend: sparse ragged rows checked entry by entry against `prompt_logprobs` top-20 (up to 1500 rows, ~15k entries, exact match), empty rows, width and row-count bounds, out-of-vocab and non-integer elements, streaming, concurrency. Both frontends accept and reject the same requests and return byte-identical matrices.
- `cargo test` (engine-core-client, text, llm, server), `cargo clippy --workspace`, `pre-commit`: pass.

## Test Result

Qwen3-8B, TP=1, 8192-token prompt, `max_tokens=1`, `int32` array input; median of 15 interleaved pairs against a ~108 ms baseline:

| rows × ids | 1000 × 64 | 4000 × 64 | 4000 × 1024 | `prompt_logprobs=0` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| added | +1 ms | +5 ms | +9 ms | +65 ms |

For 4000 rows the GPU side is ~5 ms regardless of width: the extra `lm_head` over the scored rows (~3.4 ms) and the full-vocab log-softmax (~1.4 ms). Nested-list input is slower (Python object copies); the docs recommend `int32` arrays.

## AI assistance

Implemented with Claude Code; every line reviewed by the submitter. Not a duplicate: #56860 tracks the design and #54335 is M1; no other open PR implements per-row prefill candidates.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Add output_mode to /inference/v1/generate (RFC #56851 Phase 1)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Phase 1 of #56851. A generate request can now set `output_mode: "text"` to get detokenized text next to the token IDs, so it doesn't need a separate `/derender` call. The default stays `"tokens"`, so existing clients see the same response with one new field, `output_mode`.

- `GenerateResponse` and `GenerateStreamResponse` are now unions of a tokens class and a text class, picked by `output_mode`. A body without the field still parses as tokens, so `/derender` keeps working with older responses. `/derender` now returns a 400 for text responses because a text response already has its stop string cut and decoding its `token_ids` again would put it back.
- At `text`, logprobs carry decoded tokens and `bytes`. `--return-tokens-as-token-ids` keeps the `token_id:N` placeholders.
- Text streams also send a chunk when there's new text or a finish reason but no new token IDs. That covers text held back for stop strings and the final chunk after an abort.
- `output_mode="text"` returns 400 on a server without a tokenizer or when `sampling_params.detokenize` is false.
- `/inference/v1/abort_requests` is registered wherever generate is served and requires the API key when `--api-key` is set. The unauthenticated `/abort_requests` stays `--tokens-only` only, as before.
- New docs page: `docs/serving/online_serving/token_in_token_out.md`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/ -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/test_factories.py -v
```

The new tests cover:

- protocol parsing and validation, including `/derender` rejecting text responses
- text responses and stream chunks, including chunks that only carry a finish reason or only carry text
- a text stream getting its abort chunk after `/inference/v1/abort_requests`
- abort paths: the API key protected one wherever generate runs, the bare one only with `--tokens-only`
- parity with `/v1/completions/derender`, batch and streaming, including logprobs and stop strings

## Test Result

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Suppress completion for empty pulls
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Mooncake can issue a pull with no local destination blocks only to notify the Prefill side that its producer blocks may be released. The Decode request does not wait for remote KV in this case.

`MooncakeConnectorWorker.process_pulling_result` currently reports every successful pull as `finished_recving` after its worker tasks drain. For an empty pull, this sends a completion for a request that is not in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and can trip the scheduler's request ownership/status assertion.

Empty pulls are reachable both during early-abort cleanup and when a remote prefix hit is reduced to no transferable local blocks.

## Change

Report a successful receive completion only when the pull contains at least one local destination block:

```python
if pull_meta.pull_tasks_count == 0 and any(pull_meta.local_block_ids):
    self.finished_recving_reqs.add(pull_meta.d_req_id)
```

The producer notification and pull-task accounting are unchanged. This also matches the existing failed-receive path, which already skips scheduler notification when the pull has no local blocks.

## Relationship to other work

#50565 addresses the early-abort cleanup variant by adding an explicit `notify_scheduler` flag. Its current version intentionally still reports completion for an ordinary empty-block full-prefix pull. That does not cover the case where Decode does not enter `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` after the connector returns no transferable blocks.

This PR applies the check at the worker completion sink, covering both cleanup-only and full-prefix empty pulls while preserving completion for every pull with real local destinations.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Add opt-in gfx942 MXFP4-to-int4 conversion
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Add an explicit `int4_per_group_32` MoE override for Kimi-K3 on gfx942. When selected, the MXFP4 expert weights are requantized once at load time and served through AITER's replacement BF16 x packed-int4 FlyDSL path.

The conversion is lossy and never happens by architecture alone. The default MXFP4 path is unchanged.

## Why

gfx942 does not support the scaled FP4 conversion instructions used by the native MXFP4 path. This opt-in path pays the conversion cost once during model loading and then uses the replacement packed-int4 kernels from [ROCm/aiter#4646](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4646).

## Changes

- Register `int4_per_group_32` as a MoE weight quantization key.
- Require the explicit `--quantization-config.moe.weight int4_per_group_32` override on gfx942.
- Require the replacement A16W4/int4 AITER entry point and fail closed unless it supports SiTUv2.
- Convert eight experts at a time and release each source tensor before converting the next one, bounding transient memory during load.
- Log a warning that the selected conversion is lossy.
- Leave `int4_per_group_32` out of the online MoE table so `Mxfp4MoEMethod` can convert at load time.

## Validation

Unit tests:

```text
tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_gfx942_int4.py
```

Strict AITER comparison against the torch reference passed for the production EP shape:

```text
model_dim=3584
intermediate_dim=3072
local_experts=112
topk=15
tokens=1,4,7,16,32
activation=SiTUv2
beta=4.0
linear_beta=25.0
```

Re-checked on 8x MI325X with TP8, expert parallelism, Triton RMSNorm, Triton MLA, AITER fused MoE, and full plus piecewise graph capture. Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-dc36fcce902a63eab06c1b93a5c4a5ee178a0c56` (AITER v0.1.21.post2, picked up in #55968). Serving used the replacement packed-int4 path from ROCm/aiter#4646. Current FlyDSL 0.3.2 `gemm2` cannot select `BUFFER_ATOMIC_FADD` of `v2bf16` on gfx942, so those runs used the `moe_2stage_a16wmix` kernels from ROCm/aiter#4646 on top of AITER v0.1.21.post2.

- The int4 path was FlyDSL A16W4 SiTUv2 (`ActivationType.Situv2`, `torch.int4`, `QuantType.per_1x32`, `flydsl_moe1_abf16_wint4_*`). Untuned `a16wi4` is still this path. Graph capture completed. MXFP4 native and emulation were not used.
- Chat completions returned coherent answers, including a Fibonacci Python snippet.
- 1M NIAH passed at 131072, 524288, and 1047552 tokens.
- DSpark k=7 (`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`) at 262K answered Paris, completed random chat through 250000 tokens, and passed NIAH at 65536, 131072, and 250000 with 512 output tokens. After GSM8K, 104973 of 241563 draft tokens were accepted (43.45%).
- Five-shot GSM8K through `lm_eval` `local-completions` (`num_fewshot=5`, `temperature=0.0`, `max_gen_toks=512`) scored 0.9598 strict-match and 0.9598 flexible-extract on all 1,319 questions, stderr 0.0054. That is within noise of the 0.9560 A16W4 baseline (stderr 0.0056) on the same 1,319 questions. The DSpark GSM8K run matched that 0.9598 number.
- The matched non-DSpark 262K NIAH passed the same three 512-token needles.
- `vllm bench serve` 1K input / 128 output completed 10/10 requests at concurrency 1 and 160/160 requests at concurrency 16, with no server errors. Those serving runs used the untuned FlyDSL a16w4 fallback, so they are a functional check, not a tuned peak.

## Dependency and scope

ROCm/aiter#4646 is in AITER v0.1.21.post2. vLLM picked that tag up in #55968, so this branch is no longer blocked on the AITER release.

The conversion is an explicit opt-in for deployments that accept a lossy one-time weight conversion. It does not change the default checkpoint path.

A follow-up can add `Mxfp4MoeBackend.AITER_INT4_BF16`. This PR stays on the measured FlyDSL SiTU path. It does not wait on #55684.

This PR no longer changes `vllm/config/speculative.py`. #56930 already keeps expert parallel off for non-MoE drafts such as DSpark when the target uses `--enable-expert-parallel`.

## Test plan

- [x] Quantization key and opt-in selection unit tests.
- [x] Strict production-shape comparison against the torch reference.
- [x] Full 1,319-question GSM8K after ROCm/aiter#4646.
- [x] Target-only graph capture and serving sanity.
- [x] Long-context and DSpark validation against the AITER release containing ROCm/aiter#4646.
- [x] ROCm CI on the rebased branch.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Log CRIU failure details before snapshot cleanup
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Report CRIU failure details before snapshot cleanup removes the logs. This addresses the missing diagnostics in [nightly build 92230](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92230#01a0f3da-2380-4432-9398-7da590955e0d), which reached `criu dump` after #59487 corrected the image labels.

## Claims

- Failed dump/restore commands and subprocess timeouts report bounded captured output and the end of the corresponding CRIU log.
- The original exception still propagates. Creation still deletes the unfinished artifact, and successful capture/restore follows the existing path.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_launch_cli.py -q -k 'criu_failure or preserves_bounded_criu_diagnostics or rolls_back_failed_dump'`: six passed on Mac and Linux CPU. The five new regression cases fail against the unchanged runtime; the existing cleanup test passes in both arms.

A separate Linux check used a real failing subprocess in place of CRIU and called `create_snapshot`. Its stdout, stderr and dump-log marker appeared in the console. The original exit-23 exception propagated and the incomplete artifact was removed. This checks the diagnostic path without requiring a GPU.

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Python 3.10 mypy and the Buildkite test-wiring check.

The full Mac test file has 99 passes and one environment-contract failure: CLI imports add `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=1`. The same failure reproduces on unchanged base `083060d046a8`. A broader Linux CPU run could not exercise CLI configuration cases that require a detected device; the focused diagnostics tests pass without one.

## Details

`_run` captures subprocess output, but the old CRIU path did not report that output or the CRIU log when the command failed. Creation then deleted the unpublished artifact. Collecting the file later in the CI exit trap would be too late.

The error handler reads the last 8,192 bytes of `dump.log` or `restore.log` through the existing privilege helper, with a five-second timeout. Missing or unreadable logs are reported without replacing the original failure. Captured output is also bounded, and byte-valued timeout output is decoded with replacement.

The cause of the nightly CRIU failure remains unknown. This patch makes the next attempt diagnosable; it does not claim to fix checkpoint compatibility. The regular snapshot job in [build 92059](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92059#01a0f0eb-cb9a-4998-ade5-68fe512db8f4) passed creation and both restores with identical snapshot source and E2E-driver bytes, on a different host and image.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Avoid InfiniBand state in TP1 snapshots
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the TP1 snapshot capture failure exposed by the torch-nightly job in #59487. On the affected H200, NCCL opens InfiniBand devices even for a one-rank process group. Those mappings survive the donor's sleep/reload preparation, and CRIU rejects them. This is a follow-up to #51360.

## Claims

- Default `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` only in the snapshot donor's environment. Preserve explicit caller values and use the same effective default for restore compatibility checks.
- Reject remaining open InfiniBand descriptors before CRIU, with the process, device and corrective action in the error. This does not add distributed or RDMA snapshot support.
- Fix three related audit findings: unreadable shared-memory inventory, malformed saved-remap names and false CI residue warnings before a container launch attempt.

## Validation

Reproduced on the original failing worker, `mithril-h200-4`, with one H200 and the original `593df82f33` torch-nightly image. Torch `2.15.0.dev20260928+cu130`, NCCL `2.30.7+cuda13.3`, driver `595.45.04`, kernel `6.14.0-37-generic`, CRIU `4.2.1`. The model is Qwen3-0.6B at revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, FP16, max length 512, GPU-memory target 0.50, V2 runner.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original runtime, original CI configuration | Reproduced capture failure twice. The verbose run identifies `/dev/infiniband/uverbs7`. |
| Fresh-process NCCL probe | One-rank group creation opens 24 mappings/eight descriptors. Setting `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` removes them; local all-reduce and compiled CUDA output remain correct. |
| Original full E2E with only that environment override | Passed capture and two restores across a container stop/start, including public output and cleanup checks. |
| Exact patched runtime, no external NCCL override | Passed the same full E2E. Both responses returned token 12095, text ` Paris` and logprob -0.42218855023384094, matching the captured canary. |
| Linux regression selection | Eight fail and 12 pass before the patch; all 20 pass afterward. A real unprivileged permissions probe also passes. |
| Mac snapshot selection | 93 pass. Shared argument-parser suite: 23 pass. All applicable pre-commit hooks pass. |

The complete E2E retained its 1200-second limit, cleanup reserve and correctness checks. A wrapper saved full logs before normal artifact cleanup and recorded the imported runtime hash. The patched runtime hash is `841b49f400ad974efc8ed5dc0e26eb0c9757fc98029ecc81f8c3590b80d0f489`. No host, driver or sysctl settings changed. Test containers, recorded PIDs and listeners were removed.

The focused Linux selection was `python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_launch_cli.py -q -k 'link_remap or saved_remap or cleanup_inventory or e2e_cleanup or nccl_ib or infiniband'`, using the image's installed package and a system-site-packages venv. Mac used `-k 'snapshot and not environment_contract'`. The excluded environment-contract case already fails on the unchanged base because importing AITER sets `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4`; that separate failure is not hidden or weakened here.

## Details

The reduced probe finds no IB state after Torch import or CUDA initialization. It appears at NCCL process-group creation and remains immediately after `destroy_process_group`. Disabling the unused IB transport is sufficient for this supported one-rank flow. Ordinary serving and multi-GPU transport defaults are unchanged. An explicit caller override is retained, but open IB state then causes an actionable pre-capture error. Other RDMA clients must be closed separately.

The additional hardening makes directory-read errors explicit instead of letting `Path.glob` treat them as an empty remap inventory. Restore requires the `link_remap.` filename prefix. The CI driver reports an unreadable baseline directly and checks workload cleanup only after attempting container startup. It still rejects unsuitable workers.

Open-PR searches found no duplicate of this capture repair. The broader suspend/resume proposal #35934 addresses distributed lifecycle work, not this snapshot-donor default. Thang's #59487 is still needed for nightly image labels. #59661 separately preserves CRIU failure details; it applies cleanly with this patch. Keep the nightly test enabled. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix M-RoPE offset double-count in Qwen3-Omni
commits.pr_body:
get_mrope_input_positions treated PlaceholderRange.offset as the index of the modality-start token (<|vision_start|>/<|audio_start|>), but the prompt replacement machinery only replaces the pad token, so offset points at the first pad token and the start token is already covered by the preceding text segment. The extra bos slot emitted per media item made the assembled positions one slot longer than the token span: prompts ending with a media item always hit the "Position ids length mismatch" RuntimeError (fatal to EngineCore), and prompts with trailing text got silently misaligned M-RoPE positions from the first pad token onward.

Drop the redundant bos slot and fix the st advancement in each media branch (image/audio/video/audio-in-video) so the emitted position count always equals seq_len. Add unit tests covering media-at-prompt-end for each modality and exact positions for media followed by text.



## Purpose

`Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration.get_mrope_input_positions` misinterprets `PlaceholderRange.offset`: the prompt replacement machinery only replaces the pad token, so `offset` points at the first pad token and the modality-start token (`<|vision_start|>` / `<|audio_start|>`) is already covered by the preceding text segment. The function instead treats `offset` as the modality-start index and emits an extra bos slot per media item, making the assembled positions one slot longer than the token span:

- Prompts ending with a media item (e.g. custom/transcription-style chat templates) always hit `RuntimeError: Position ids length mismatch with input ids length`, which is fatal to EngineCore.
- Prompts with trailing text (stock chat template) don't crash, but every M-RoPE position from the first pad token onward is silently misaligned by one slot — a correctness bug on all multimodal requests.

This drops the redundant bos slot and fixes the `st` advancement in each media branch (image/audio/video/audio-in-video) so the emitted position count always equals `seq_len`. The audio-in-video value structure (shared bos/eos positions) is preserved, consistent with the Qwen2.5-Omni behavior in HF.

Follow-up to GHSA-328w-h674-qp56 (per maintainer feedback, the crash path requires an operator-chosen chat template; this PR fixes the offset handling itself).

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py -v
```

New unit tests use synthetic input_ids + `MultiModalFeatureSpec` (no GPU/weights needed):
- `test_mrope_positions_{image,audio,video,audio_in_video}_at_prompt_end`: prompt ending exactly at the modality-end token must yield `positions.shape == (3, seq_len)`.
- `test_mrope_positions_image_then_text`: media followed by text must produce the exact expected per-position values.

## Test Result

Before the fix: all 5 tests fail — the 4 media-at-prompt-end cases raise `RuntimeError: Position ids length mismatch` (the engine-death path), and the image-then-text case fails on misaligned position values.

After the fix: all 5 tests pass.

commits.pr_title: [EPLB] Add contention-aware expert migration batching
commits.pr_body:
Partially addresses #31671.

## Summary

During async EPLB, several expert weights can be transferred through the same rank and NIC at once. These traffic bursts compete with inference and can increase serving latency.

This change adds an opt-in scheduler that groups migrations by source and destination rank, then splits them into batches. In each batch, a rank communicates with at most one peer, while independent rank pairs still transfer concurrently. Expert weights still move one layer at a time, but schedules for all MoE layers are prepared once per rebalance cycle to reduce Python overhead.

`enable_migration_batching` remains `false` by default. Setting it to `true` enables the new path only when `use_async=true`; synchronous EPLB always keeps the existing path because inference is paused and serial batches would extend the pause. NIXL transfer context is restored before every batch because `execute()` drains it.

I checked open EPLB migration/scheduling PRs and found no duplicate implementation. AI assistance was used; I (a human contributor) reviewed every changed line and am responsible for the contribution.

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/parallel.py \
  vllm/distributed/eplb/async_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py \
  vllm/distributed/eplb/migration_scheduler.py \
  vllm/distributed/eplb/rebalance_execute.py \
  tests/distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py
```

Result: `12 passed`; selected pre-commit hooks passed.

## End-to-end serving benchmark

One four-node run used Ubuntu 22.04.5, one Quadro RTX 6000 24 GB GPU per node, Ray 2.56.1, NIXL 1.3.2 over 10 GbE without RDMA, and prefix caching enabled. The model was `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507` with TP=4 and 32-way concurrency. Each case used a fresh server; 500/500 requests completed.

Server command:

```bash
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507
USE_BATCHING=true  # repeat with false
EPLB_CONFIG="{\"window_size\":50,\"step_interval\":50,\"num_redundant_experts\":32,\"log_balancedness\":false,\"use_async\":true,\"communicator\":\"nixl\",\"enable_migration_batching\":$USE_BATCHING}"

vllm serve "$MODEL" --dtype float16 --port 8000 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb --eplb-config "$EPLB_CONFIG" --enforce-eager
```

Bench command:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model "$MODEL" --port 8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-prefix-len 300 \
  --random-input-len 200 --random-output-len 300 \
  --num-prompts 500 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 0 --temperature 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,99 \
  --ignore-eos --disable-tqdm --save-result \
  --result-dir "$RESULTS" --result-filename bench.json
```

| Batching | Duration (s) | Request/s | Output tok/s | TTFT P50/P99 (ms) | TPOT P50/P99 (ms) | E2EL P50/P99 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| off | 4,756.10 | 0.1051 | 31.54 | 49,180.71 / 75,740.25 | 828.53 / 1,007.82 | 303,462.69 / 322,184.88 |
| on | 4,650.17 | 0.1075 | 32.26 | 48,599.04 / 74,756.17 | 812.44 / 999.01 | 293,821.76 / 317,351.61 |

Async batching improved request throughput by 2.28%, TTFT P50/P99 by 1.18%/1.30%, TPOT P50/P99 by 1.94%/0.87%, and E2EL P50/P99 by 3.18%/1.50%.

The head node's total network traffic (bytes received + bytes transmitted) was sampled from Linux byte counters once per second; it is not a `vllm bench serve` metric. NIC P99 decreased from 599.81 to 538.40 MB/s (10.24%). The plots and unmodified JSON/log files are in [`results/serving_nixl_20260911_async_random500`](https://github.com/DOCCA0/vllm/tree/ilp/benchmarks/eplb_rebalance/results/serving_nixl_20260911_async_random500).

![End-to-end improvement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DOCCA0/vllm/ilp/benchmarks/eplb_rebalance/results/serving_nixl_20260911_async_random500/e2e_improvement.png)

![NIC traffic over time](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DOCCA0/vllm/ilp/benchmarks/eplb_rebalance/results/serving_nixl_20260911_async_random500/nic_timeseries.png)

## Scheduler profiling

The profiling run used the same server and workload parameters, with only NVTX-only Nsight capture enabled. The exact commands are documented in [`COMMANDS.md`](https://github.com/DOCCA0/vllm/blob/ilp/benchmarks/eplb_rebalance/results/serving_nixl_20260911_async_random500_profile/COMMANDS.md). Open the four [`rank*.nsys-rep`](https://github.com/DOCCA0/vllm/tree/ilp/benchmarks/eplb_rebalance/results/serving_nixl_20260911_async_random500_profile/trace) files with Nsight Systems 2024.5.1 or newer and search for `eplb: schedule migration batches`.

Each range is one scheduler call covering all 48 MoE layers in a rebalance cycle, rather than one call per layer. The transfers themselves remain layer-by-layer. The measured per-rank results were:

| Rank | Calls | P50/call (ms) | Total time across all calls (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 34 | 7.819 | 302.081 |
| 1 | 34 | 7.090 | 253.152 |
| 2 | 34 | 7.035 | 255.239 |
| 3 | 34 | 7.005 | 241.190 |

The four ranks schedule concurrently, so their times are not added. Across the 34 cycle-wide scheduler calls, rank 0 had the largest measured total scheduling time: 302.081 ms. The independent clean A/B benchmark completed 105.932 s faster with batching. Comparing these two measured values gives a scheduler-cost-to-serving-time-saved ratio of 0.285%.

![Scheduler cost versus serving time saved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DOCCA0/vllm/ilp/benchmarks/eplb_rebalance/results/serving_nixl_20260911_async_random500_profile/scheduler_cost_vs_saved.png)

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build][NVIDIA] Build Rubin images on the public nvidia/cuda base image
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Build the Rubin (CUDA 13.4) images on the conventional public `nvidia/cuda:13.4.1-base-ubuntu24.04` final image instead of `nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda-dl-base:26.08-cuda13.4-devel-ubuntu24.04`, and remove the Dockerfile workarounds that only existed for the NGC / internal prerelease base images and wheels.

**Base image (docs + release pipeline)**
- `FINAL_BASE_IMAGE=nvidia/cuda:13.4.1-base-ubuntu24.04` in the Rubin build instructions (`docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md`) and in both CUDA 13.4 Rubin nightly steps of `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml`. Drop the doc note that claimed a `devel` final image is required: the cu134 PyTorch nightlies now pull the CUDA libraries as pip dependencies (`cuda-toolkit[...]==13.4.1`), and the Dockerfile already installs the JIT toolchain (`cuda-nvcc`, `cuda-nvrtc-dev`, `libcublas-dev`, ...).
- Build Rubin images with `NCCL_VERSION=2.32.3`, the first NCCL release with Rubin (SM107) support. The NGC image bundled NCCL; the bare CUDA image does not, so NCCL now comes from `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.32.3` through the existing `UV_OVERRIDE`.

**Dockerfile cleanup**
- Remove the `ENV CUDA_VERSION=${CUDA_VERSION}` normalization (the NGC image sets a four-component `CUDA_VERSION=13.4.1.012`).
- Remove the runtime `/usr/lib/libnccl.so.2` symlink for NCCL bundled in the base image, and the GDRCopy skip when the base image already ships `libgdrapi` (GDRCopy is installed the same way as for non-Rubin images again).
- Remove DeepEP's `EP_NCCL_ROOT_DIR=/usr` override that pointed at the builder image's NCCL. DeepEP now builds against the pip `nvidia-nccl-cu13==${NCCL_VERSION}` like every other build.
- Remove the `libcurand.so.11 -> libcurand.so.10` alias and the `/opt/venv/lib` / `nvpl/lib` `ld.so.conf` entries. They served the internal prerelease PyTorch wheel: the public cu134 nightlies neither link nor dlopen libcurand (all public CUDA 13.x curand is `.so.10`), and the aarch64 wheel bundles NVPL under `torch/lib` with an `$ORIGIN` RPATH.

**FlashInfer / quack / CUTLASS DSL / PyTorch**
- FlashInfer 0.7.0 (#58069) and quack-kernels 0.6.5 are now in `requirements/cuda.txt` for everyone, so drop their pins from `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt` along with `flashinfer-jit-cache`, `flashinfer-cubin` and the FlashInfer extra indexes. Rubin now installs them through the same path as non-Rubin builds: the Rubin skip around the `flashinfer-jit-cache` step is removed, and so is the Rubin-only `sed` that stripped pins from `requirements/cuda.txt`.
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` `4.7.1` -> `4.8.0` in `requirements/cuda.txt`, for every CUDA build. Rubin previously pinned `4.8.0.dev0` separately in `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt`; that pin is removed, so CUDA 13.0 and Rubin CUDA 13.4 images now ship the same CuTe DSL. See the GB200/GB300 A/B below.
- PyTorch nightly -> `2.15.0.dev20260928` (x86_64) / `2.15.0.dev20260926` (aarch64), torchvision `0.30.0.dev20260928`, torchaudio `2.11.0.dev20260928`. The torch pin stays per-architecture because the aarch64 torchvision `0928` wheel requires torch `0926`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the Rubin final base image, NCCL version or Rubin dependency pins. #58765 touches the same `flashinfer-jit-cache` RUN step (switching it to `flashinfer download-kernels` while keeping a Rubin bypass); whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase, and after this PR that bypass is no longer needed.

Note: the FlashInfer JIT-cache index is derived from `CUDA_VERSION` for Rubin too (`cu134`). `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt` is CUDA 13.4-specific, so no other Rubin CUDA version is expected to work with it.

## Test Plan

Built the `vllm-openai` target with the documented Rubin command (plus `INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true` to cover the release-pipeline configuration) on both architectures:

```bash
docker buildx build --progress=plain --load --file docker/Dockerfile --target vllm-openai \
  --platform linux/${ARCH} --build-arg max_jobs="$(nproc)" --build-arg nvcc_threads=2 \
  --build-arg RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false --build-arg INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE=true --build-arg INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true \
  --build-arg TRITON_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE_REPO=https://github.com/triton-lang/triton.git \
  --build-arg TRITON_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE_REVISION=3f6e41132b5edf639bfb872ad73d4688765e08b8 \
  --build-arg CUDA_VERSION=13.4 --build-arg BUILD_BASE_IMAGE=pytorch/manylinux{aarch64,2_28}-builder:cuda13.4 \
  --build-arg FINAL_BASE_IMAGE=nvidia/cuda:13.4.1-base-ubuntu24.04 --build-arg NCCL_VERSION=2.32.3 .
```

- x86_64 build on an R100 host (driver 620.16); aarch64 build on a VR200 host (driver 610.47.04, CUDA 13.3 UMD, no forward-compat env needed).
- Image checks: expected versions installed (torch/vision/audio nightlies above, flashinfer-python/cubin/jit-cache 0.7.0, cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, quack-kernels 0.6.5, `nvidia-nccl-cu13` 2.32.3 and vLLM logs `nccl==2.32.3` at runtime), `import deep_ep`/`flashinfer`/`cutlass`/`quack` succeed, `libgdrapi` present, CUDA works on the GPUs, and no torch/torchvision/torchaudio shared object has unresolved dependencies after removing the curand/NVPL loader entries.
- Served each model with `vllm serve` in the image, sent chat requests (and an image request for the VL checkpoints), and ran `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 250` (5-shot completions). Baseline = the NGC-based `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-{x86_64,aarch64}` from main (36768d1b) with the same flags.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files.
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.8.0 A/B on GB200/GB300, see below.

## Test Result

All chat answers were correct and coherent (e.g. "The capital of France is Paris.", `17*23 = 391`, a correct `is_prime`, a correct Rayleigh-scattering explanation) and the VL models correctly described the test image (a stop sign in front of a Chinatown archway).

| 4x VR200 (aarch64) | nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 | TP=4 | auto (FLASHINFER_TRTLLM) | 0.860 | 0.844 |
| 4x VR200 (aarch64) | nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 | TP=4 + EP | auto (FLASHINFER_TRTLLM) | 0.844 | — |
| 4x VR200 (aarch64) | nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 | TP=4 | `flashinfer_cutedsl` | fails ² | — |
| 4x VR200 280 GB (aarch64) | MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 (BF16) | TP=4 | auto (FlashInfer CUTLASS) | 0.868 | — |

This reproduces identically on the NGC-based nightly, so it is independent of this PR. commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Support fp8 combine in FlashInfer one-sided MoE all2all
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
Forwarding fp8 combine flag to increase perf when low precision is supported in FlashInfer combine

## Test Plan
Use GB300 cluster to A/B test with and without the flag `VLLM_FLASHINFER_MOE_A2A_LOW_PRECISION_COMBINE` on, using DeepSeek-R1-0528 NVFP4, 8k input / 1k output.

## Test Result
- For the microbenchmark, there is a small gain at DEP8 (2–8 us per dispatch+combine, about 1–2%), mixed at DEP4. I ran this with just DeepSeek R1 shapes and a sweep across tokens per rank (benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe_a2a_combine.py)
- Then I did the serving with nsys (DEP4 and DEP8): the combine kernel is about 17% faster on decode-sized calls but slower on large prefill-sized calls. The fp8 kernel uses 191 registers per thread vs 96 for bf16, could be causing slowdown due to spilling for prefill-sized ones.
- I also tried serving without the profiler, DEP8 (2 nodes); fp8 gave +4.0% output throughput and 2.7% lower median ITL vs bf16. I ran that over 4 server launches (bf16, fp8, fp8, bf16) to balance the order with the benchmark running 3 times each.
- Had a small issue in one of the runs because one of fp8 runs hung shortly after the profiler was stopped. No run hung without the profiler.

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This changeset attempts to use the recently added CuteDSL MegaMoE kernels from FlashInfer to accelerate large batch size (prefill mostly) inference. We will evaluate on several models to exercise as many paths as possible.

It is effectively a generalization of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49636 beyond DeepSeekV4.

## Test Plan

To test this feature, we evaluate accuracy against baseline with the GSM8K eval and we measured performance using `vllm bench serve` in simulated prefill scenarios (setting OSL to 1), where these kernels should excel. We chose a variety of models to attempt to cover as many code paths as possible.

All runs were performed on 4xGB200 whenever possible. For DeepSeekV4 Pro, we instead ran on 8xB200.

The servers were started with variations of the following, adjusted per model:

**Baseline server**

```bash
vllm serve \
  $MODEL_PATH \
  --served-model-name evaluation-model \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --language-model-only --enforce-eager \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_cutedsl \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --seed 42 --port 8000
```

**Candidate server**

```bash
vllm serve \
  $MODEL_PATH \
  --served-model-name evaluation-model \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --language-model-only --enforce-eager \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --seed 42 --port 8000
```

Benchmarking load was generated with:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions --model evaluation-model \
  --tokenizer $MODEL_PATH \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 \
  --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 1024 --num-warmups 256 \
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Avoid generation for empty streaming input
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the case where a streaming-input generator ends without yielding any chunks.

vLLM creates a placeholder request while setting up the stream. Previously, if the stream ended before sending its first chunk, that placeholder was submitted to the engine as a real generation request.

This change tracks whether any input chunk was submitted:

- If at least one chunk was submitted, the existing final-request behavior is unchanged.
- If the stream ends normally without any chunks, `STREAM_FINISHED` is placed directly on the output queue.
- If the input stream raises an error, the existing `InputStreamError` is preserved.

This was split out of #53861 following review feedback. It does not overlap with #58941 or #58942, which cover the collector-boundary and abort/session-race fixes.

## Test Plan

Added a regression test that verifies an empty input stream:

- Returns `STREAM_FINISHED`.
- Does not submit the placeholder request to the engine.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Watermarking] Keep draft prompt lengths valid under CUDA graphs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix stale prompt lengths in the draft watermark deduplication mask under CUDA graphs. The bug came in with #56807. I found it while reviewing #59554, which would expose DFlash to it too.

## Claims

- With `dual_key_gumbel` and the default `deduplicate_contexts="single_turn"`, draft sampling under FULL CUDA graphs (default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) read prompt lengths from a stale UVA buffer after new requests arrived. This affects EAGLE3, MTP and DSpark (reproduced; EAGLE shares the autoregressive path). Some drafts were sampled without key A where they should carry it, and some repeated contexts were not deduplicated. Graph and eager mode now agree.
- No host sync, and no end-to-end change I can separate from run-to-run noise (see Performance). The fix adds one async copy of `max_num_reqs` int32 values per propose. The captured dedup kernel then reads device memory instead of pinned host memory, which is faster in a microbenchmark.

## Validation

Engine harness: Qwen3-4B targets (Qwen3.5-0.8B for MTP) with dedup `single_turn`. It compares the dedup mask each draft row actually used against a CPU reference built from the true prompt lengths. Compared with the engine-level script under Reproduction, it also covers Poisson arrivals, MTP and DSpark. λ is arrivals per engine step.

| Workload | Before (FULL graph) | After (FULL graph) | Eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 K=3, crafted (one request at a time, prompt-copying) | 576/1905 mask rows wrong; 536 accepted drafts lacked key A | 0/1896 | 0/1896 |
| EAGLE3 K=3, online Poisson (λ=0.2, mean concurrency 12) | 43/23178 mask rows wrong (41 falsely skipped, 2 missed dedup) | 0/23178 | 0/23325 |
| MTP K=3, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 32.6% / 2.06% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |
| DSpark K=7, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 39.5% / 2.05% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |

The MTP and DSpark "after" numbers come from the harness's patched `prepare()`, not from a commit tree. The EAGLE3 online "after" rows used the first revision of this fix, which differed only in copying into a `[:num_reqs]` slice. The EAGLE3 crafted "after" and eager runs use this commit.

Host sync: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, EAGLE3 under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, 12 staggered admissions and 98 `prepare()` calls: clean. A deliberate `.item()` in `prepare()` trips the check, so the check does cover this path.

Unit test:

```bash
pytest tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py -k reads_current_prompt_lens   # fails on main, passes with the fix
pytest tests/watermarking/                                                    # 148 passed (B300)
```

The test is CUDA-only. CI runs `tests/watermarking` only in the CPU "V1 Others" step, where it is skipped. I ran it locally on a B300: it fails on main and passes with the fix, and the suite passes (148).

About 1-2% of accepted drafts are affected at low traffic (EAGLE3 0.98%, MTP 2.06%, DSpark 2.05%) and 0.54% when busy (EAGLE3). Per-category detection rates in paired runs are identical for EAGLE3 and within noise for MTP and DSpark: at most 2 of 19-20 requests differ. The bug still breaks the watermark's own contract, and graph and eager runs diverge.

### Performance

Setup: B300, Qwen3-4B with EAGLE3 (`AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3`, K=3, probabilistic), `dual_key_gumbel`, temperature 1.0, random 1024 in / 256 out with `--ignore-eos` (64 prompts at c=1 and c=8, 256 at c=64), default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Main and fix servers ran in parallel on two GPUs, swapped each round, for 10 rounds of 2 passes. Δ is the mean of the per-round paired change, ± the 95% CI. A/A is the same comparison of main against main (4 rounds).

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (main → fix) | Δ tok/s | Δ mean TPOT | Δ mean TTFT | Acceptance length | A/A Δ tok/s | A/A Δ TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 464.7 → 462.3 | −0.5% ± 0.6 | +0.5% ± 0.6 | +1.8% ± 2.0 | 1.632 → 1.632 | −0.4% ± 0.6 | +0.6% ± 3.4 |
| 8 | 3032 → 3012 | −0.6% ± 0.8 | +0.4% ± 0.9 | +2.3% ± 1.7 | 1.658 → 1.662 | −0.3% ± 3.3 | −1.2% ± 5.6 |
| 64 | 10543 → 10495 | −0.4% ± 0.8 | +0.3% ± 0.9 | +0.8% ± 1.5 | 1.533 → 1.533 | +0.3% ± 1.2 | −0.7% ± 4.1 |

Throughput and TPOT change by less than 1%, with CIs that include zero. The A/A differences are of similar size.

Mean TTFT is 0.35-0.65 ms (0.8-2.3%) higher. Only the c=8 CI excludes zero (+0.7% to +4.0%). Between two identical main servers, per-round TTFT differences range from −6% to +3%, and one A/A CI (c=64 acceptance length) also excludes zero. I read the TTFT difference as noise, but these runs cannot rule out a TTFT cost of a few percent at c=8.

`prepare()` alone, with a UVA-backed prompt-length source and the speculator's two gathers: host time goes from 48.4-48.9 µs to 51.4-52.1 µs (+3 µs for one more copy launch). The copy itself takes 4.2 µs on the GPU at `max_num_reqs=1024` and 0.9 µs at 256. The dedup kernel runs once per draft step, so three times per propose at K=3. Replayed in a CUDA graph, those three steps get faster because the kernel reads device memory instead of pinned host memory: 12.3 → 8.7 µs with 1 request and 30.2 → 17.0 µs with 1024 requests (`max_num_reqs=1024`).

### Reproduction

A standalone script shows the bug without a model. It captures the draft dedup mask in a CUDA graph, admits a request (which moves `prompt_len.gpu` to the next pool buffer), and compares the replayed graph with eager mode. Run it on a CUDA GPU with `python repro_stale_prompt_len.py`.

<details>
<summary>repro_stale_prompt_len.py</summary>

```python
# Draft watermark dedup mask under a CUDA graph reads a stale prompt length.
import torch

import vllm
from vllm.v1.watermarking.gumbel import GumbelWatermarker
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils import UvaBackedTensor

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
dev = torch.device("cuda")
wm = DraftWatermarker(GumbelWatermarker(key=42, context_width=2), max_num_reqs=1,
                      device=dev, num_speculative_steps=1,
                      deduplicate_contexts="single_turn",
                      deduplicate_contexts_max_history=None)
prompt_len = UvaBackedTensor(1, dtype=torch.int32)  # like req_states.prompt_len
# Request in slot 0: prompt [5, 6, 9], generated [5, 6], next draft context
# [5, 6]. The context repeats only inside the prompt, so with single_turn the
# draft must use key A. Read with prompt length 0, it looks like repeated
# generated text and the draft skips key A.
tokens = torch.tensor([[5, 6, 9, 5, 6]], device=dev)
total_len = torch.tensor([5], device=dev)
ctx = torch.tensor([[5, 6]], device=dev)
enabled = torch.tensor([True], device=dev)
logits = torch.zeros(1, 8, device=dev)
idx = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
temp, draft_step = torch.ones(1, device=dev), torch.tensor(0, device=dev)

def prepare():  # the speculator calls this on every propose()
    wm.prepare(ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_len.gpu, total_len)

def uses_key_a():  # per-row mask that draft sampling uses for key A
    return wm._sampling_state(logits, idx, temp, draft_step, ctx)[1]

prepare()  # capture time: slot 0 has prompt length 0
uses_key_a()  # warm up outside capture
graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
    graph_out = uses_key_a()
# A step that admits a request runs copy_to_uva(), which moves
# prompt_len.gpu to the next buffer of its round-robin pool.
prompt_len.np[0] = 3
prompt_len.copy_to_uva()
prepare()
eager = uses_key_a().item()
graph.replay()
replayed = graph_out.item()
print(f"eager: key A={eager}  graph: key A={replayed}  ->",
      "OK" if eager == replayed else "STALE prompt length in graph")
```

</details>

Main:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=False  -> STALE prompt length in graph
```

With the fix:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=True  -> OK
```

An engine-level script runs EAGLE3 with `dual_key_gumbel` through `LLM`, admits 24 requests one at a time, and counts draft rows whose dedup mask differs from the mask built from the current prompt lengths. Run `python engine_repro.py` for the default CUDA graph mode and `python engine_repro.py eager` for eager mode (30-45 s each on a B300).

<details>
<summary>engine_repro.py</summary>

```python
# EAGLE3 + dual_key_gumbel: compare the dedup mask each draft row used with the
# mask recomputed, in the same CUDA graph, from the current prompt lengths.
import os
import sys

import torch

os.environ.update(VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER="1", VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING="0")
import vllm  # noqa: E402
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker as DW  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.watermark import draft_watermarking_mask  # noqa: E402

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
orig_init, orig_prepare, orig_state = DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state
instances = []

def __init__(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args):
    orig_init(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args)
    self.true_pl = torch.zeros(max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    self.stats = torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)  # rows, wrong, skip
    instances.append(self)

def prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens):
    orig_prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens)
    self.true_pl.copy_(prompt_lens)  # current prompt lengths

def _sampling_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx):
    steps, mask = orig_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx)
    ref = draft_watermarking_mask(
        self.all_token_ids, idx, self.true_pl, self.total_lens, self.prior_contexts,
        ctx, steps, self.enabled[: len(ctx)] & (temps != 0),
        self.deduplicate_contexts_max_history, False)
    self.stats += torch.stack(
        [torch.ones_like(ref).sum(), (mask != ref).sum(), (ref & ~mask).sum()])
    return steps, mask

DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state = __init__, prepare, _sampling_state
wm = {"algorithm": "dual_key_gumbel", "key": 42, "context_width": 4}
spec = {"method": "eagle3", "model": "AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}
llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-4B", speculative_config=spec, watermark_config=wm, seed=0,
          max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
          enforce_eager=sys.argv[1:] == ["eager"])
(dw,) = instances
dw.stats.zero_()  # drop warmup and capture rows
text = ("The committee met on Tuesday to review the annual budget. The members agreed "
        "to fund the public libraries, repair the old bridge near the river, and hire "
        "two more nurses for the clinic. The mayor promised a full report next month.")
for i in range(24):  # one request at a time; each admission rotates the UVA pool
    ask = f"Repeat exactly, word for word:\n{text}" if i % 3 == 1 else "Say hi."
    llm.chat([{"role": "user", "content": f"[{i}] {ask}"}],
             SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, seed=i, max_tokens=96), use_tqdm=False,
             chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False})
rows, wrong, skipped = dw.stats.tolist()
print(f"draft rows={rows}  mask rows wrong={wrong}  wrongly skipped key A={skipped}")
```

</details>

| Run | Output |
|---|---|
| Main, CUDA graphs (2 runs, identical) | `draft rows=714  mask rows wrong=129  wrongly skipped key A=129` |
| Fix, CUDA graphs | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Main, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Fix, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |


## Details

**Root cause:** `req_states.prompt_len` is a `UvaBackedTensor`. `copy_to_uva()` runs from `apply_staged_writes` on steps that add requests, and it moves `.gpu` round-robin across the buffer pool. `DraftWatermarker.prepare()` stored that reference, so a captured `draft_watermarking_mask` kept reading the capture-time buffer. Newly admitted requests then see the previous occupant's prompt length until the pool comes back around:
- If the stale length is shorter than the real one, prompt n-grams count as generated history and the draft skips key A.
- If it is longer, real repeats are missed.

**Fix:** `DraftWatermarker` owns an int32 `[max_num_reqs]` buffer, and `prepare()` copies into it. This follows the existing `contexts` and `enabled` copies in the same method. It is also the principle MRV2 states for fused draft decoding: replayed tensor state must live in persistent storage.

I found no other inputs to captured draft sampling that go stale:
- `all_token_ids` and `total_len` are `StagedWriteTensor`s whose `.gpu` never moves.
- `contexts` and `enabled` are already copied into owned buffers.
- Other UVA-backed inputs to the draft path (temperature, seeds) are already copied into speculator-owned buffers. The remaining readers run eagerly.

**Unchanged behavior:** eager mode and the watermark-off path are unaffected. By code inspection, dedup modes `none` and `all` do not depend on prompt lengths: `none` returns before the mask is built, and `all` searches from position 0. The copy still runs in those modes; its cost is negligible.

**Alternatives:**
- Making `RequestState.prompt_len` a stable `StagedWriteTensor` would fix this for every future graph reader. It touches the penalties, bad_words, trace_replay and model_runner readers, and the `LogitsProcessor` interface types `prompt_len` as `UvaBackedTensor`, so it is better done as a separate refactor.
- A persistent device mirror inside `UvaBackedTensor` would cost a copy for every user.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Constrain non-strict GLM-4.7 tool calls with a shallow structural tag
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix GLM-4.7-family tool calling when strict tool calling is disabled.

When `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0` and no tool is marked `strict: true`, the glm47 parser currently falls back to unconstrained generation. This means `auto`, `required`, and named tool choices can emit malformed GLM tool-call XML or arguments that do not follow the provided tool schema.

This PR adds a non-strict structural tag for the non-strict GLM tool-calling path. The constraint is built and registered in `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py` (like `kimi_k3` and `hy_v4`, which use the same XML pattern), instead of hand-written grammar rules in the parser file.

The tag constrains the post-reasoning assistant output rather than only the tool arguments. It covers:

- normal assistant text (with GLM structural tokens excluded);
- one or more GLM `<tool_call>` blocks;
- tool names from the request;
- shallow argument typing derived from each tool's JSON schema.

For example, instead of allowing the model to freely generate the native GLM tool syntax, the parser installs a structural tag that constrains the output shape while still allowing normal reasoning and text before tool calls. The thinking prefix stays owned by the engine-side reasoning gate, matching the contract of the existing strict structural-tag path.

### Request handling

`Glm47MoeModelToolParser.adjust_request()` now attaches this tag when:

- tools are provided;
- `tool_choice != "none"`;
- `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING` is disabled;
- no tool is explicitly `strict: true`;
- no structured output / response-format constraint is already present.

Existing strict-tool behavior is unchanged and continues to use the xgrammar `glm_4_7` builtin.

Named tool choice is narrowed to the selected tool (via `normalize_tool_choice`), while `auto` and `required` use the available request tools. Both Chat Completions and Responses API tools are supported, including Responses API namespace tools.

### Structural tag registry builder

`get_glm_4_7_structural_tag` is registered under `"glm_4_7"` in `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py`:

- schema-exact mode (`non_strict=False`, the existing strict-tool path) delegates to the xgrammar `glm_4_7` builtin. The delegation rebuilds the builtin's input protocol from the normalized tools (normalize is idempotent and has already filtered `"forced"` down to the named tool) and is verified byte-identical to the previous dispatch across {auto, required, named} x {strict, non-strict} tool sets (6/6 cases).
- non-strict mode (`non_strict=True`) builds shallow tags from the same composable formats the other vLLM builders use (`TagFormat` / `TriggeredTagsFormat` / `TagsWithSeparatorFormat` / `StarFormat` / `OrFormat` / `AnyTextFormat`): tool names are constrained, argument keys may be omitted / repeated / emitted in any order, values are typed shallowly (strings are raw text excluding GLM structural tokens, other types are bare JSON scalars, enums enumerate), and free text cannot contain GLM structural tokens.

Because the constraint is a regular structural tag, the existing plumbing is reused end-to-end (xgrammar compile path, reasoning gate, spec-decode rollback, bitmask application). No Responses API protocol or serving changes are needed; the diff stays inside the parser and the registry.

## Scope

The change only affects the glm47 parser family when strict tool calling is disabled, plus a mechanical signature extension (`non_strict: bool = False`) for the builders registered in the structural tag registry and the harmony builder.

The existing paths remain unchanged for:
- `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=1`;
- tools with `strict: true`;
- requests with an explicit structured output;
- requests with an explicit JSON response format;
- requests without tools;
- `tool_choice="none"`.

There are no model, scheduler, kernel, sampling, or tokenizer changes.

## Performance

A/B on a GLM-4.7-format model (TP=8 H100, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0`), 12 sequential requests per case; "valid" = structured `tool_calls` returned with no markup leakage:

| Case | main (unconstrained) | This PR (non-strict tag) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required`, valid tool calls | **0 / 12** (raw JSON leaks into `content`) | **12 / 12** |
| `required`, latency median | 0.51 s (garbage output) | 0.41 s |
| `auto`, valid tool calls | 12 / 12 | 12 / 12 |
| `auto`, latency median | 0.36 s | 0.37 s |
| `auto`, decode throughput | 186 tok/s | 185 tok/s |
| `required` streaming TTFT / total (median) | 0.08 s / 0.50 s | 0.08 s / 0.27 s |

Constraint overhead measured offline with the `zai-org/GLM-4.7` tokenizer: tag build ~0.8-10 ms; cold xgrammar compile 12-20 ms (compiled asynchronously in the engine); cached re-compile ~0.1 ms; compiled spec 2.6-15 KiB for 2-12 tools. No measurable latency or throughput regression on the auto path; the required path additionally goes from unusable to fully functional.

## Test Plan

Unit tests (run locally):

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py -q      # 19 passed
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -q    # passed (part of the 315 below)
```

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/ -q   # passed
```

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py \
        tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py \
        tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
        tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py -q                     # 315 passed

pytest tests/parser -q \
  --ignore=tests/parser/mistral \
  --ignore=tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py \
  --ignore=tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py                   # 786 passed

pytest tests/v1/structured_output -q \
  --ignore=tests/v1/structured_output/test_mistral_common_tokenizer.py   # 72 passed
```

Structural-tag validation with the tokenizer via `GrammarCompiler.compile_structural_tag` + `GrammarMatcher`: valid turns (text + tool calls) are accepted; `<tool_call>` markup inside text, wrongly typed argument values (e.g. a string for an `integer` param), invalid enum values, and unknown tool names are rejected; omitted / reordered / repeated arguments are accepted (non-strict semantics); named choice narrows to the selected tool and rejects others; EOS and turn-taking stop tokens stay selectable.

End-to-end (GLM-4.7-format model served with `--tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45`, TP=8 H100, MTP speculative decoding `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0`), 8/8 scenarios pass:

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tool_choice="auto"` non-strict tools | well-formed `tool_calls`, `finish_reason="tool_calls"`, no markup leakage |
| `tool_choice="required"` | well-formed `tool_calls`; e.g. `{"city": "Beijing", "days": 3}` with correct integer typing |
| named tool choice (Chat Completions) | only the selected tool is called, `finish_reason="stop"` per OpenAI semantics |
| named zero-argument tool | zero-arg call parsed as `"{}"` |
| no tools | plain text answer, no markup |
| `enable_thinking=false` | grammar-structural validity: single text block, no `<think>`/`<tool_call>` leakage |
| streaming (SSE) | deltas assemble the same tool call, clean finish |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back and answered normally |

No "Failed to advance FSM" errors appeared in the server logs across all runs.

Note: this change is output-format constrained decoding only (grammar-guided); model weights and sampling defaults are untouched, so no accuracy evaluation delta is expected beyond the format guarantees above.
